responsive.title: Responsive Collaborator
responsive.summary: Rewards engineers who reply fast, reply often, and whose feedback moves PRs to merge. In a repo shipping ~300 human PRs a day, a person who unblocks others quickly is the scarce resource.
responsive.formula: impact = 0.40 × Responsiveness + 0.40 × Volume + 0.20 × Merge follow-through (each a percentile rank 0-100 among eligible engineers)

factors.label: Responsiveness
factors.metric: Median reply latency in hours across the engineer's responses

factors.label: Volume
factors.metric: Number of responses (issue comments, inline review comments, reviews)

factors.label: Merge follow-through
factors.metric: Median hours from the engineer's last comment on a PR to that PR merging

definitions: Response event: a human's issue comment, inline review comment, or review (APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED, DISMISSED, or COMMENTED with a non-empty body) on a PR or issue. Empty COMMENTED reviews are dropped because they only wrap inline comments that are counted separately.

Trigger: for a response at time t on an item, the most recent human event on that item before t by someone other than the responder, or the item's creation if there is none. Bot events never count as triggers.

Reply latency = response time minus trigger time. Excluded when the previous human event on the item is by the same person (a follow-up, not a reply) or when the item predates the window with no in-window trigger. Volume still counts these.
Merge follow-through, per (engineer, merged PR) where the engineer is not the author: merged_at minus the engineer's last event before merge.
Human: GitHub user type is User and the login is not on the bot denylist (matches [bot], ends in bot, or is in the configurable list shown below).
Percentile rank: each factor is converted to 0-100 among eligible engineers. 92 on responsiveness means faster than 92% of eligible peers.
thresholds: Eligible: at least 20 responses and at least 10 distinct PRs or issues in the window.
Window: 90 days ending at ingest time. Items count if created or updated in the window; only events created in the window are stored.
External contributors are included and labeled with their author association (MEMBER, CONTRIBUTOR, ...).
PRs authored are shown as context on each card but are not part of either score.
Merge follow-through needs at least 5 merged PRs the engineer commented on; otherwise it is dropped and the weights renormalize to 0.50 responsiveness / 0.50 volume, and the card says so.
Reply latency and follow-through deltas are capped at 14 days before taking the median.
limitations: Latency is wall-clock, so weekends and time zones inflate it. The median blunts this but does not remove it.
First-response latency on a PR is measured from PR creation, not from 'ready for review' or a review request. Draft PRs are flagged and their creation-to-first-response latency is excluded.
Comments in Slack, pairing sessions and design docs are invisible to this data.

constructive.title: Constructive Communicator
constructive.summary: Rule-based scoring of each comment's substance, with no sentiment and no LLM. It asks one question: does this comment give the reader something to act on?
constructive.formula: impact = 0.50 × Comment quality + 0.30 × Substantive volume + 0.20 × Breadth (each a percentile rank 0-100 among eligible engineers)

factors.label: Comment quality
factors.metric: Mean per-comment quality q (0-1) across the engineer's responses

factors.label: Substantive volume
factors.metric: log(1 + number of responses with q ≥ 0.4)

factors.label: Breadth
factors.metric: Distinct people whose PRs or issues the engineer responded on

definitions: Per-comment quality q (0-1) adds points for: substance (0.30: 15+ words after stripping quotes and code = full, 5-14 words = half), code (0.20: a fenced code block or GitHub suggestion block), reference (0.15: a URL, #1234 reference, or file path / line reference), question (0.10: at least one '?'), actionable phrasing (0.15: should / could / consider / suggest / instead / what if / nit / let's / we can / try), rationale (0.10: because / since / so that / otherwise / leads to / this causes).
Ritual-only override: a body that is only lgtm / +1 / thanks / done / nice / emoji is forced to q = 0.

Response event: a human's issue comment, inline review comment, or review (APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED, DISMISSED, or COMMENTED with a non-empty body) on a PR or issue. Empty COMMENTED reviews are dropped because they only wrap inline comments that are counted separately.

Trigger: for a response at time t on an item, the most recent human event on that item before t by someone other than the responder, or the item's creation if there is none. Bot events never count as triggers.
Human: GitHub user type is User and the login is not on the bot denylist (matches [bot], ends in bot, or is in the configurable list shown below).
Percentile rank: each factor is converted to 0-100 among eligible engineers. 92 on responsiveness means faster than 92% of eligible peers.
thresholds: Eligible: at least 20 responses and at least 10 distinct PRs or issues in the window.
Window: 90 days ending at ingest time. Items count if created or updated in the window; only events created in the window are stored.
External contributors are included and labeled with their author association (MEMBER, CONTRIBUTOR, ...).
PRs authored are shown as context on each card but are not part of either score.
A response counts as substantive when q ≥ 0.4.
limitations: Algorithm B rewards length and structure as proxies for substance. A long unhelpful comment scores well; a terse brilliant one scores poorly.
Latency is wall-clock, so weekends and time zones inflate it. The median blunts this but does not remove it.
First-response latency on a PR is measured from PR creation, not from 'ready for review' or a review request. Draft PRs are flagged and their creation-to-first-response latency is excluded.
Comments in Slack, pairing sessions and design docs are invisible to this data.

bestComments.itemTitle: refactor(frontend): move toolbar to lemon components
bestComments.excerpt: The root cause is that `person_id` is resolved after the override table is read, so overrides written in the same batch are missed. Two options: (1) read overrides in the same transaction, (2) re-order the steps. I'd suggest (2) because it avoids a lock — see `plugin-server/src/worker/ingestion/person-state.ts:210`. What do you think?

fastestReplies.itemTitle: fix(dashboards): tile refresh race when filters change
fastestReplies.excerpt: What happens if `snapshot_chunks` is empty? I think we'd throw on line 112 — consider guarding and emitting a `replay_missing_chunk` event so we can measure it.

bestComments.excerpt: Nice — one thing: the `useEffect` runs on every filter change, so the tile refetches twice when both the date and breakdown change together. Consider debouncing via `useDebouncedCallback` from `lib/hooks`; we did the same in `trendsDataLogic` and it removed the double query.
